title: Refraction: how light bends in glass
goal: See how the angle of refraction depends on the angle of incidence and the refractive index, and when light cannot leave a medium.
note: A ray of light bends when it enters a denser medium. The refractive index n is sin i divided by sin r. A larger n bends the ray more, and inside the medium there is a critical angle above which the light cannot get out.

graphs.title: The angle of refraction rises with the angle of incidence but stays smaller than it.
graphs.label: Angle of refraction

experiment.aim: To find how the angle of refraction depends on the angle of incidence
experiment.hypothesis: The larger the angle of incidence, the larger the angle of refraction
controlled: The refractive index of the medium

sentences: Going from air into a denser medium, the ray bends towards the normal, so the angle of refraction is smaller than the angle of incidence.
The critical angle belongs to the medium: light inside it that meets the boundary at a larger angle is totally internally reflected.
steps: Keep the refractive index at 1.5, set the angle of incidence to 20, then press Record.
Set the angle of incidence to 40, then press Record.
Set the angle of incidence to 60, then press Record.
Compare the angle of refraction with the angle of incidence each time.

predict.prompt: Light enters glass from air. How will the angle of refraction compare with the angle of incidence?
predict.reveal: Set the refractive index to 1.5 and the angle of incidence to 40, then compare the two angles.

concept_check.question: What happens to the angle of refraction if the refractive index rises and the angle of incidence stays the same?
concept_check.explanation: The refractive index is sin i divided by sin r, so a larger index means a smaller sin r: the ray bends more towards the normal.
